name: security-cms-signed-content-binding-review
intent: CMS signed object, signer purpose and consumed-content binding
artifacts: CMS parser/verifier version, signer trust/EKU policy, signed attributes and application object selection.
trace: Trace the verified signer and signed bytes to the exact document/action consumed, including detached content and duplicate/ambiguous structures.
experiment: Use an isolated fixture with owned certificates and synthetic documents; compare rightful signer/content and a wrong-purpose or mismatched content object.
disproof: A mathematically valid signature is not application signer authorization; a displayed certificate subject is not proof of trust.
repair: Bind accepted signer purpose and content representation to the consumer and verify valid signed workflows.
branch_decisions: Resolve attached versus detached content, signed attributes, signer certificate purpose and the exact object the consumer uses. A cryptographically valid signer may not be trusted for this operation. Unsigned outer metadata or an alternate embedded object must not replace verified content; compare intended signed data and a harmless alternate object in an offline fixture.
operational_method: Select the CMS signedAttrs branch explicitly. For id-data, signedAttrs may be absent; verification then covers the content-octet path defined by the profile, so do not reject that valid form merely for lacking attributes. When signedAttrs is present, validate required content-type/message-digest attributes, their agreement with selected content and the specified signed-attribute encoding; non-id-data requires signedAttrs. Retain the actual verifier-selected signer/content and consume that verified result, not an unsigned outer alternative. An embedded certificate is not automatically an authorized signer. Compare valid id-data without attributes with an attributed-content mismatch and a wrong-purpose signer offline.
